items.title: RI1FJL homeward bound: yacht clears Franz Josef Land
items.blurb: Slava OK8AU (via UA6GG): after QRT, the team boarded the yacht at 0030 local and set course for Murmansk; they have already left the ZFI archipelago into a storm. Cabins were about 5 °C with condensation everywhere when they loaded; sailors had waited two weeks. Two Spiderbeams broke on the last day but were repaired — huge pileups, no polar bears, walruses and icebergs only.

items.title: 3W9C on Hòn Sơn: 6 m yagi up, HF VDA online
items.blurb: Jack SP5APW reports he is on Hòn Sơn (AS-128): a 4-el 6 m yagi yielded 100-plus contacts, then a tri-band VDA for HF. After a power outage and RFI hiccup right after the VDA went up, he is QRV on 20 m FT8 with a clear shot to North America. Europe should try the long path — hills block the short path. Last 3W9C before his Vietnamese license expires.

items.title: 5W0AF Samoa confirmed: Apia from 21 September, SSB only
items.blurb: Jacek SP5EAQ refreshes the postponed Samoa trip: QRV from Apia as 5W0AF starting 21 September for three weeks, SSB only on 10–40 m (80 m possible in the last week). QSL via SP7DQR OQRS; bureau cards and LoTW free; logs online at least once a day. Middle East airspace disruption had pushed the original March plan to autumn.

items.title: RI1FJZ: daily Club Log/LoTW on island; on-air eyed ~13 September
items.blurb: Vasily RA1ZZ: internet for Alexandra Island is sorted, so Club Log and LoTW uploads will be daily for donors, sponsors, and OQRS. Special paper QSLs to EU/AS/NA optimized at USD 6; LoTW-only remains an option without mailing. Team still looks for about 13 September on the air after the weather-slipped Murmansk sail.

items.title: K0NR and K0JJW start a Lewis and Clark Trail POTA run
items.blurb: Bob K0NR and Joyce K0JJW left St. Louis on 5 September in their Class B van Rocky for a mid-October Pacific finish along the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail (POTA US-4572). Plan is opportunistic SSB and FT8 on 20/17/15 m plus 2 m FM, camping parks tied to the Corps of Discovery. Spots may be last-minute — watch for K0NR.

items.title: ANS-249: AMSAT Board voting under 10%, closes 15 September
items.blurb: Today's AMSAT News Service notes fewer than 10% of eligible members have voted in the 2026 Board election. Five candidates for three seats: KD2CQ, N8MH, KK5DO, N8HM, and N6UA. Current members cast ballots at launch.amsat.org; results by 30 September. If you meant to vote, the clock is short.

items.title: ISS amateur radios down Monday for Progress undocking
items.blurb: ARISS ops note in ANS-249: Service Module radio powers down about 1210Z Monday 7 September and Columbus at 1215Z ahead of Progress undocking ~1516Z; both return about 1905/1910Z. Crossband repeater stays 145.990 up (PL 67) / 437.800 down when live. No school contacts on the board this week; HamTV is still on a test signal.

items.title: ARRL posts Perseus22 SDR crowded-band review in Learning Center
items.blurb: ARRL asks how the Microtelecom Perseus22 SDR holds up in real-world crowded band conditions and points members to the full video in the ARRL Learning Center. Fresh morning post with the usual #hamradio tag — useful if you are shopping wideband HF SDRs or comparing front-end behavior.
